subject: Hospitality
title: Dynamic Pricing Explained
description: A 60-second lesson on Dynamic Pricing Explained.

hook.text: The same hotel room might cost $150 on Monday and $350 on Saturday. Dynamic pricing adjusts rates constantly based on demand.

buildup.text: Factors include day of week, season, local events, competitor pricing, booking pace, and how many rooms are left unsold.

discovery.text: When a big conference comes to town, nearby hotels raise rates weeks in advance as their algorithms detect rising demand.

twist.text: Dynamic pricing means loyalty doesn't guarantee a good rate. The same guest pays differently every visit based on market demand.

climax.text: Hotels update prices multiple times daily. The room you saw for $200 this morning might be $250 by tonight.

punchline.text: Same room, different days, different prices. Welcome to dynamic pricing.

quiz.question: What drives dynamic pricing in hotels?
options: Demand factors like events, day of week, season, and competitor rates
